edge_explainer.we_believe: Organic growth is genuinely ~11% (they publish the bridge), the leverage 'cap' is self-imposed guidance with a real de-lever track record — NOT a covenant — and the governance cleanup (super-voting shares eliminated) removes a real discount. The founder bought ~$50M of stock in the open market at/below today's price.
edge_explainer.why_we_might_have_edge: The one EVIDENCED counterparty claim in our book: the founder (now former CEO) bought ~$50M of stock in the open market at and below today's price — a named, informed actor on our side of the trade, verified on SEC Form 4s. The complexity argument (Up-C, preferred, acquisition accounting) cuts BOTH ways — it fooled our own first pass (we initially mis-stated the tax liability), so we claim only that we have now reconciled it, not that others can't.
edge_explainer.why_it_might_be_priced_in: The honest math says MOSTLY it is: our own conservative fair value ($43) sits BELOW the price ($49). Cash conversion is only ~4% of adjusted EBITDA after interest, preferred dividends, and capex — the market may be correctly charging for a roll-up whose EBITDA is an accounting object. That's why this is a 6/10 and we now enter only AFTER the print.
